text:
yasmin: Quick design huddle: thinking through pool picker/pinning, typeahead behavior, and undo for autoscale changes. Prototype live: https://figma.com/file/abc. Need opinions on keyboard flow and how we surface a single recommended pool without breaking search.
otto: I like a lightweight "Suggested" chip above the list (not a full row). It should be actionable (click to select) but not steal focus on open. Typeahead should still land in list items, not the chip.
claire: Sketch attached shows 3 states: (1) No suggestion (normal list) (2) Suggested chip visible (compact) (3) Expanded suggestion row with rationale + apply button. We can A/B test compact vs expanded.
yasmin: For accessibility we must ensure the chip is reachable by keyboard (tab) but not the default arrow navigation. People expect arrow keys to go through results.
otto: Implementation note: make chip tabbable with tabindex=0 and set role=button, but on dropdown open, call focus() on search input; arrow keys should move through list only. That keeps typeahead consistent.
claire: Microcopy options for the chip: "Suggested pool" vs "Recommended for this workload". Which is concise and clear?
tom: "Suggested pool" is short and less prescriptive. "Recommended" can feel like an override. Also add one-line reason under the chip: e.g., "Lower P99 for short requests".
ux-bot: Accessibility lint: 1) when chip appears after search, announce it via aria-live as "Suggested pool available" 2) ensure chip has aria-describedby pointing to the rationale 3) avoid relying on color alone.
yasmin: Undo/confirmation for apply-from-suggestion: do we show a toast with undo or a modal confirmation for large changes? My take: smaller changes = toast+undo (5s), larger changes (capacity > X or reserved contracts) = modal with explicit acknowledgement.
otto: Agree. Also add a lightweight audit entry when someone applies a suggestion: capacity.change.applied with actor and reason. That helps Support.
claire: Visual density question: do we show min/max steppers inline with pool row or hide behind an "edit" affordance? Inline is faster but noisy. Compact view could collapse steppers to an expansion panel.
yasmin: Preference for inline on desktop, collapsed on mobile. We should expose a compact toggle in settings for power users.
tom: Backend constraint: if we allow transactional apply (suggestion apply) we need a single API endpoint that accepts {poolId, changes, tag: suggestionId}. That lets us attach telemetry and rollback. Also define rollback window server-side (e.g., 10s) to allow client undo.
otto: UX detail: when user types to filter, and a suggested chip matches the query, do we keep the chip visible or hide it? My instinct: keep visible above results if the query is a prefix match. If mismatch, hide it.
claire: That feels natural. Also for keyboard, if user presses down immediately after opening, focus should go to the first list row, not the chip. Tab should reach chip first if user is tabbing.
ux-bot: Accessibility note: when applying a suggestion that changes min GPUs, emit an aria-live update: "Minimum GPUs set to N. Undo available." For modal confirmations use role="alertdialog" correctly.
yasmin: Copy choices for the undo toast: "Change applied. Undo" vs "Autoscale setting updated — Undo". Preference?
otto: Shorter is better in toast: "Settings updated — Undo". Keep the verb tense consistent.
tom: Also decide on telemetry event names: capacity.suggestion.clicked, capacity.suggestion.applied, capacity.change.undone. Add tags: poolId, actorId, suggestionId, delta. Sam from infra will refine schema.
yasmin: One more edge: Dedicated customers with reserved capacity cannot reduce below reserved floor. If a suggestion would drop below reserved, we should disable apply and show tooltip: "Cannot apply — reserved capacity floor." Also provide link to contract docs.
claire: UX for disabled apply: show disabled button with info icon and tooltip. Make sure tooltip is keyboard accessible.
otto: For the typeahead performance, debounce at 150ms and show optimistic matches locally until server returns full list. Avoid flicker by keeping previous list visible while loading.
yasmin: Final decisions for now: - Show a top 'Suggested' chip (label: "Suggested pool") with one-line reason; chip tabbable but arrow keys ignore it. - If user clicks apply on chip, show toast with Undo (10s) for small changes, modal for large/reserved-impacting changes. - Audit & telemetry events for apply/undo. - Keep steppers inline on desktop, collapsed on mobile/compact mode. - Ensure aria-live messages for suggestion availability and for applied changes.
claire: I'll update the frames with the chip variant + expanded row variant and include keyboard flow notes.
otto: I'll scope the component changes: tabbable chip, aria-live announcements, role=button, ensure typeahead arrows skip chip. PR coming tomorrow.
tom: I'll draft API contract for apply/rollback and reserved-floor checks.
ux-bot: Reminder checklist: 1) chip role & aria-describedby 2) aria-live for suggestion show/hide and apply 3) keyboard skip semantics for arrow keys 4) toast Undo accessible via keyboard.
yasmin: Great work. I'll collate follow-ups and add to the design task. If anyone wants to push more microcopy options, drop them in the figma comments. Thanks! :sparkles:
